content:
maria: Heads-up — planning a mid-tier slab refresh in us-east-3 this Saturday 03:00-06:00 UTC. This is a staggered node reboot + NIC firmware bump across 3 racks. Expected steady-state GPU capacity drop ~8% for ~2h during the window.

alex: Is this touching Dedicated pools or only hosted burst/spot capacity?

maria: Only mid-tier (burst + spot-backed tenant classes) — Dedicated and private VPCs NOT touched. We'll mark racks as drainable before reboot.

sam: What about model-serving SLAs that pin to us-east-3? Any automated routing/fallback?

maria: We'll enable policy-based routing to steer traffic to eu-west1 and us-west2 for pinned routes. Canary path will be to eu-west1 for 10% of traffic then ramp.

jen: How do we handle KV cache warmup for the biggest seq models? Seeding takes time and impacts latency.

maria: Plan: pre-seed hot prefixes on backfill nodes 45m before each rack is fully drained. Script: 

```
# preseed kv cache (example)
./kv-preseed --zone=us-east-3 --rack=rack-12 --prefixes-file=top1000.txt --parallel=6
```

sr e_lead: Add network hedging — do a transient BGP weight shift to reduce cross-region bursts during the handoff. We shouldn't overload eu-west1 links.

alex: Are we assuming extra egress costs for region steering? Need an estimate to sign off with finance.

maria: Back-of-envelope: estimated egress + spot backfill delta ~$6k for the 3h window (includes preseed traffic). Will attach detailed cost breakdown to the runbook.

sam: Any concerns about tenant eviction or fairness for long-running GPU jobs? Can we use a temporary priority bump to avoid noisy eviction storms?

maria: We'll set tenant-throttle policy: non-critical long-running tasks get a soft-throttle instead of hard kill. Also will advertise temporary shorter TTL on scheduling decisions to speed rescheduling.

infra-bot: Reminder: create the maintenance incident in incidents channel and link the runbook (runbook id: rb-2026-193). Also add alert suppression for known noisy signals (gpu_temp and nvlink flaps).

jen: Who's owning canary verification and perf signoff? Need traces from endpoints + token-level latency breakdown for top 5 models.

maria: @sam you own canary perf verification. @alex you'll own Dedicated routing rules check (even tho not touched, validate fallbacks). I'll own cost + runbook text and comms.

sam: Got it. I'll create a quick smoke harness: 50 concurrent requests for gpt-l/long and embed-ml200, compare p50/p95 to baseline.

alex: Product comms — do we want a proactive email to customers in us-east-3 or only status page? Some enterprise tenants require 72h notice.

maria: Send targeted enterprise comms (72h) + public status page notice (48h). I'll loop in support to triage any tenant questions during the window.

jen: One more ask — include a quick rollback plan if we see NVLink error rates spike after firmware bump.

maria: Rollback plan in runbook: if nvlink-error-rate > 0.3% sustained for 10m, revert NIC fw on the cohort and failback traffic. Escalation matrix included.

infra-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: maintenance/7260002222. Slack thread pinned.

sam: I'll post canary results 30m after the start of the window. If anything looks off, I'll abort and escalate.

maria: Thanks team. Final checklist: preseed scripts ready, BGP weight change runbook validated, incident created, cost estimate in runbook, enterprise comms queued. Anyone else?

alex: thumbs-up. :thumbsup:

jen: I'll run the NVLink health sweep tonight on the candidate racks and share results tomorrow morning.

maria: Perfect — closing planning here unless someone raises new blockers.
